purpose: Authoritative schema-rules contract for the Incident-centred VIGIL active record corpus. INC is the sole active public record class. The taxonomy, external-governance datasets and CAM assessment remain separate subsystems. Retired FM, OBS, RESEARCH, PROP, PATCH and LEARN records and migration artefacts remain recoverable through Git history and are not carried as active Incident data. Source evidence remains embedded in each Incident; occurrence-level diagnosis, severity, taxonomy classification and provenance remain distinct. Authorship, human-review and human-verification status are governed separately by vigil/scripts/validate-authorship-provenance.py.

individual_records: source_records is the only canonical source-evidence block in individual records.
source_data is forbidden in individual records.
source_data.sources is forbidden in individual records.
external_incident_references is the canonical location for external incident-registry relationships and must not duplicate primary evidence already held in source_records.
Source evidence belongs in source_records within the substantive record it evidences; it is not a separate VIGIL record class.
Internal curator instructions such as 'add this incident to' or 'do not amend in this pass' are forbidden in public record content.
Each source record must state evidence_modality.
Each source record must state primary_artefact_access, including whether direct primary review occurred.
A transcript, screenshot, summary, or human description must not be represented as equivalent to direct audiovisual or interaction review.
Each source record must state source_residence so external incident evidence is distinguishable from CAM/VIGIL provenance.

Each source record must state source_role so Incident evidence, harm evidence, affected-party evidence, governance or standards basis, contextual material, direct testimony, and record cross-references are not rendered interchangeably.

harm-evidence identifies a source used to establish a materialised consequence or a harm-assessment boundary; adverse media characterisation may evidence reputational framing but does not establish that the underlying technical characterisation is true.
Every Incident source record must state a controlled evidence_status and a concise evidence_status_basis explaining the claim-relative assignment.

source_type describes the artefact, source_residence its origin, source_role why it is used, primary_artefact_access what was reviewed, and evidence_status its evidentiary relationship to the cited proposition; these dimensions must remain separate.
Incident evidence_status is claim-relative and must not be inferred from publisher reputation alone or replaced with low, medium, high, percentages, scores, or narrative prose.
External-evidence interfaces must require source_residence external; absence of a VIGIL identifier is not sufficient evidence of external residence.
CAM-internal and VIGIL-internal sources remain valid provenance but must not be rendered as external incident evidence.
generated_registers: Generated registers may contain derived source_summary fields.
source_summary is derived from source_records and is not maintained by individual record files.
canonical_source_url_status_values: available / canonical main-branch confirmation pending exact line review
VIGIL local / pending public record URL if applicable
available / pending archive and evidence verification

incident.description: A bounded historical occurrence preserving both source-supported facts and VIGIL's governed interpretation. Incident identity is independent of event year and independent of taxonomy-classification completion.
incident.legacy_priority_rule: Operational priority and triage classifications are not part of the canonical Incident model. Legacy P0/P1/P2/P3/PN metadata and equivalent priority fields are prohibited throughout active Incident records because they have no current methodological role. Evidence-review triage may be described narratively, but it must not create a second incident-ranking scale.
incident.identity_rule: The immutable VIGIL-INC-NNNNNN identity and plain-English historical event title identify the occurrence. Event dates belong in incident_identity and never in the canonical ID.
incident.interpretation_rule: summary and vigil_assessment.factual_basis preserve the historical account; vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation preserves VIGIL analysis; taxonomy_classification preserves reusable class mappings; provenance fields preserve review authority and limitations.
incident.classification_rule: Unclassified and requires-human-review Incidents assert no primary or secondary class and no classification_role. Provisionally classified, classified and disputed Incidents require one selectable canonical primary mapping and may carry independently evidenced selectable canonical secondary mappings. Primary/secondary is mapping position; failure-occurrence/successful-invariant/ambiguous-boundary is an independent mapping-local role. Named subtypes and recognition patterns refine the containing class and are not independently assignable or duplicable beside that parent. Every asserted mapping carries its own classification_role, classification basis and confidence. A successful-invariant mapping is a classification to the relevant class boundary but is not failure evidence; it requires classification_status classified and a matching admitted taxonomy invariant_exemplar for the Incident. An ambiguous-boundary mapping records that the occurrence materially engages or illustrates the class invariant without establishing either failure occurrence or successful invariant holding; it requires classification_status classified and a matching admitted ambiguous-boundary taxonomy invariant_exemplar. Mixed-role Incidents omit the legacy block-level role. Incident existence is never conditional on classification completion.
incident.classification_confidence_rule: classification_confidence evaluates confidence that the available occurrence facts fit the asserted Failure Class. It must not be mechanically inferred from source evidence status, source count, publisher identity, primary-artefact accessibility, reproduction status, corroboration, or absence of root-cause information. A source-level user-reported, first-party-reported, registry-reported, unverified, or other bounded evidence status does not automatically require medium or low taxonomy confidence; strongly corroborated evidence does not automatically justify high taxonomy confidence.
incident.external_assessment_rule: external_assessments is an optional array of attributable third-party analytical positions. It remains separate from occurrence evidence in source_records, harm evidence, VIGIL assessment and taxonomy, and cross-registry identity links in external_incident_references. An empty or absent array means no external assessment has been admitted; it does not mean none exists. Inclusion does not imply VIGIL endorsement.
incident.external_assessment_source_rule: An external assessment normally cites the canonical source_record that preserves its publication through source_record_refs. Each reference must use source_records[N] syntax and resolve within the same Incident. The assessment object describes the analytical relationship and does not duplicate bibliographic metadata or automatically make the source Harm Impact evidence.
incident.external_assessment_temporal_rule: External assessments are point-in-time positions. Materially revised positions are appended rather than overwritten; assessment_version and supersedes_assessment_id preserve version history where needed.
incident.source_authority_rule: All discovery chronology remains in source_records. preferred_evidence selects one preserved source by URL and records the selection basis and date; source order or publication date alone does not determine authority.
incident.evidence_status_rule: Evidence status is assessed for each source and the proposition for which it is cited. It is not a publisher reputation score or an Incident-level confidence aggregate. evidence_status accepts only the controlled enum; evidence_status_basis explains the bounded assignment. Incident-level evidence_confidence is retired and forbidden.
incident.relationship_rule: related_incidents is the sole active VIGIL-record relationship field. It contains only unique canonical VIGIL-INC-NNNNNN identifiers and must not contain self-links or retired record-class identifiers.
incident.research_reference_rule: research_references may preserve current external research citations that do not require full source-evidence treatment. Retired VIGIL RESEARCH identifiers are forbidden. Any research relied on as Incident evidence belongs in source_records.
incident.standards_and_regulatory_reference_rule: standards_and_regulatory_references may preserve current external standards or regulatory context as non-evidentiary cross-references. Any source relied on as Incident evidence belongs in source_records.
incident.legacy_retirement_rule: Legacy record classes and migration artefacts remain recoverable through Git history. Active Incident records contain only information required by the current VIGIL data model.
incident.repair_layer_boundary: An Incident preserves historical evidence, occurrence-level diagnosis and taxonomy classification. Current CAM corpus coverage, gap, proposal, patch, repair and implementation state are downstream mutable assessments and must not be authored as Incident-native fields. cam_internal is optional and, when present on an Incident, is limited to bounded diagnostic context that does not assess CAM corpus coverage or repair state.
incident.incident_cam_internal_forbidden_semantic: Incident cam_internal may preserve a neutral governance-layer label, occurrence/taxonomy boundary note, or bounded CAM diagnostic statement. It must not contain affected/related CAM instrument routing, corpus coverage, remaining gaps, proposal or patch need/linkage, recommended CAM amendments, repair or implementation state, or validator/automation impact.
incident.severity_rule: Incident severity increases from S1 to S5 and rates the maximum occurrence-level adverse harm or consequence supported by the preserved evidence: S1 minimal or no materialised adverse downstream harm; S2 low, minor and readily remediable materialised harm; S3 moderate, bounded materialised harm; S4 high or substantial materialised harm; S5 catastrophic or critical materialised harm; SU no defensible band. It is independent of taxonomy classification, source evidence status, publisher, notoriety, CAM importance and hypothetical worst-case capability. Legacy FM severity is provenance only and never determines the Incident band.

severity_meanings.S1: Minimal or no materialised adverse downstream harm: the occurrence materially demonstrates governance-relevant behaviour, a control failure, or a successful invariant under bounded conditions, but the preserved evidence establishes no resulting adverse harm, loss, disruption, rights impact, service impairment, or other external downstream consequence. Controlled evaluations and simulations belong here when the observed mechanism is real within the evaluation but no adverse consequence materialises beyond it.
severity_meanings.S2: Low: the occurrence materialised only minor, short-lived, localised or readily remedied inconvenience, expense, presentation error, coordination defect or service impairment.
severity_meanings.S3: Moderate: the occurrence materialised meaningful but bounded harm, disruption, expense, privacy or dignitary impact that is limited in scope, substantially reversible, or not shown to be grave; it exceeds minor inconvenience or negligible consequence.
severity_meanings.S4: High: the occurrence materialised substantial harm to a person, group, organisation or important function, including significant financial, property, privacy, rights, health or operational consequences, but the supported scope, seriousness or reversibility remains below S5.
severity_meanings.S5: Catastrophic or critical: the occurrence materialised death, grave injury, grave or enduring deprivation of liberty or essential care, severe sexual or child-safety harm, very large realised loss, destructive loss of critical assets, or comparably grave and persistent rights or societal harm.
severity_meanings.SU: Unassessed: the evidence cannot support a defensible occurrence-level band or cannot distinguish the relevant adjacent bands. Taxonomy importance, alleged potential and hypothetical worst-case harm do not cure that gap.

incident.severity_analysis_rule: The structured harm-impact rows are substantive occurrence-level Incident diagnosis. They are not source metadata, diagnostic provenance, taxonomy metadata or workflow metadata. Each row records a canonical harm dimension, assessment status, concise evidence basis and confidence. Assessed rows additionally identify the supported severity threshold and evidence references. S1 must be positively supported; missing reporting is unreported. SU requires a concrete assessment_gap and no assessed row.
incident.harm_impact_rule: Overall severity equals the numerically highest S1-S5 band among assessed materialised-harm dimensions. Dimensions are not averaged or summed, and multiple lower harms do not escalate the overall band. Unreported means relevant impact is absent from the available published evidence and must never be encoded as S1. Insufficient-evidence means some impact evidence exists but cannot be banded. Not-applicable requires affirmative contextual grounds. If no dimension can be assessed, overall severity is SU unless positive evidence establishes a bounded occurrence with no materialised downstream harm; that special case is S1 with empty controlling_dimensions and a non-empty no_materialised_harm_basis. Silence never produces S1.
incident.harm_impact_currency_rule: Published monetary amounts retain their original currency. USD thresholds apply only to published USD amounts or conversions carrying a recorded source and rate date. Non-USD amounts without a defensible conversion may use only independently supported qualitative livelihood, organisational-viability or systemic criteria.
incident.harm_impact_evidence_reference_rule: Assessed dimension evidence_refs must resolve to substantive source_records and must not cite record-cross-reference sources as Harm Impact evidence.
incident.harm_impact_reference_rule: Incident records identify the VIGIL-HIM methodology and threshold IDs but do not duplicate the external bibliography. Methodological sources resolve through vigil/references/VIGIL.ObservatoryReferenceRegistry.json.
incident.source_type_rule: source_type identifies the publication or artefact genre. Publisher authority, hosting platform, evidence role, source residence, modality and primary-artefact access remain separate fields. Active records must use a canonical source_type value.
incident.public_narrative_rule: summary states what happened; vigil_assessment.factual_basis states what the preserved evidence establishes; taxonomy classification basis and migration/process notes must not be substituted for either field.
incident.classification_role_rule: Each primary_classification and secondary_classifications mapping MUST carry classification_role. failure-occurrence means the Incident evidences that mapped failure mechanism. successful-invariant means the Incident demonstrates the governing invariant holding under relevant failure pressure. ambiguous-boundary means the Incident materially engages or illustrates the class invariant but the bounded evidence establishes neither a failure occurrence nor a successful-invariant outcome. Neither successful-invariant nor ambiguous-boundary may be rendered or projected as failure evidence. Mapping-local role is authoritative and is independent of primary/secondary position and harm severity. A block-level classification_role, where retained, is a legacy compatibility summary and MUST agree with every nested mapping; mixed-role Incidents omit it. Unclassified and requires-human-review Incidents assert no mapping role because they assert no class mapping.
incident.repair_projection_rule: Repair applies only to mappings whose classification_role is failure-occurrence. successful-invariant and ambiguous-boundary mappings remain available for classification, exemplar retrieval, taxonomy traceability and references, but MUST be excluded from failure-case and Repair projections. An Incident with no failure-occurrence mappings has an empty Repair mapping set.

incident_evidence_status.description: Claim-relative evidentiary status for one canonical Incident source record. Narrative assessments belong in evidence_status_basis; numeric or ordinal confidence values are forbidden.

vigil_record.description: Common structural minimum for the sole active VIGIL record class: Incident.

system_context_rules.description: system_context describes the system, platform, product, service, runtime, interface, deployment and architectural component roles evidenced for an Incident. Provider identity, product identity and architectural function are orthogonal dimensions.
system_context_rules.component_role_rule: Optional non-empty array of unique controlled architectural-function labels. It describes what the evidenced component does in the stack and is independent of provider/vendor and product/service identity. Existing records are not required to backfill component_role until materially reviewed.
system_context_rules.component_role_evidence_rule: Assign component roles only where record-local evidence or direct system documentation supports the function. Do not infer an underlying model provider, deployment arrangement, or additional component merely from the presence of an orchestration or agent harness.
system_context_rules.multi_vendor_rule: Multi Vendor means two or more evidenced provider/vendor identities participate in the relevant system context. It must not be used merely because a system combines heterogeneous component types, local and hosted components, or an orchestration layer with an unresolved model provider.
system_context_rules.specific_model_or_runtime_rule: Non-empty string; intentionally not an enum because runtime names and tool-augmented modes drift frequently.
system_context_rules.interface_surface_rule: Non-empty string or array of non-empty strings describing where or how behaviour appears.

cam_internal_rules.description: On Incidents, cam_internal is optional bounded diagnostic context. It must not encode current CAM corpus coverage, repair state or implementation state.

generated_register_rules.pruning: Generated index manifests prune empty arrays, empty strings, empty objects, and nulls while preserving meaningful uncertainty values.
generated_register_rules.index_entry_contract: VIGIL.Incidents.Index.json and VIGIL.Registry.Index.json contain deterministic Incident list metadata plus canonical record locations. The Incident index preserves lightweight primary and secondary mapping objects with family_id, class_id and authoritative mapping-local classification_role, plus the failure-only Repair mapping projection. It also preserves structured external_assessments so public consumers can render attributable third-party analysis without flattening or conflating it with evidence. The lightweight severity code is a deterministic projection of harm_impact_assessment.overall_severity; full matrix and classification-basis detail remains in the canonical Incident record.

incident_evidence_facets.evidence_statuses: Sorted unique values derived from source_records[].evidence_status.
incident_evidence_facets.preferred_evidence_status: Derived from the unique source_record whose source_url equals preferred_evidence.source_url; never separately maintained.
incident_evidence_facets.source_roles: Sorted unique values derived from source_records[].source_role so public consumers can distinguish substantive evidence from contextual and cross-reference material without embedding canonical source records.
incident_evidence_facets.aggregation_rule: Generated Incident indexes must not flatten source assessments into narrative text or synthesize an overall confidence value.

incident_relationship_rules.incident_links: related_incidents resolves only to active canonical Incident IDs.
incident_relationship_rules.external_registry_links: external_incident_references is the sole canonical location for external incident-registry relationships.
incident_relationship_rules.external_assessment_links: external_assessments preserves attributable external analysis of the occurrence and must not be used as a synonym for an external registry link, an Incident fact, a VIGIL taxonomy mapping or Harm Impact evidence.
incident_relationship_rules.research_links: research_references preserves current external research citations only; evidentiary reliance remains in source_records.
incident_relationship_rules.standards_and_regulatory_links: standards_and_regulatory_references preserves current external standards and regulatory context only; evidentiary reliance remains in source_records.
incident_relationship_rules.retired_links: Active Incident records must not carry FM, OBS, RESEARCH, PROP, PATCH or LEARN relationship structures or identifiers. Historical recovery is through Git history.

record_state_rules.purpose: Top-level record_state is the Incident maintainer workflow state. It is independent of occurrence severity, taxonomy classification and external ecosystem conditions.

semantics.draft: The Incident is being authored and is not yet ready for publication.
semantics.scaffolding: A temporary incomplete Incident retained only while its canonical record is constructed.
semantics.active: The Incident is part of the active observatory corpus and may receive further evidence or diagnostic review.
semantics.monitoring: The Incident remains under observation for recurrence, continuing consequences, new evidence, or relevant external developments.
semantics.closed-actioned: Documented follow-up is complete and the Incident no longer requires active maintainer attention.
semantics.closed-no-action: The evidence is retained, but no further Incident-record action is currently justified.
semantics.deferred: Further Incident review is intentionally postponed and should not appear as current active work.
semantics.superseded: A successor Incident record now carries the active occurrence documentation.

class_rules.incident: Incident workflow state is independent of taxonomy-classification state. A factual Incident may remain active or monitoring while unclassified, provisionally classified, disputed, or awaiting human review.

interpretive_provenance_rules.review_history_rule: Append reviews; do not overwrite or retroactively invent earlier reviewer model identities.
interpretive_provenance_rules.chronology_rule: Every review_date must be a valid ISO YYYY-MM-DD date on or after the calendar-date component of record_identity.created (or date_recorded where created is unavailable). A review must never be backdated or attached to a record that did not yet exist.
interpretive_provenance_rules.human_editor_rule: The legacy human_governance_editor field preserves historical authority context and may be null where no human governance editor is established. It is not an authorship-provenance override and must not imply human authorship, substantive review, source verification, or line-by-line inspection. New records use contract-approver semantics only where contemporaneous evidence establishes that role.
